spec_features.spec_quote: the agent a **first-class, dignified exit**: it can stop and say "I'm blocked"
spec_features.evidence: finish tool defined (tools.py:73-86) and dispatched returning is_finish (tools.py:124-130). In loop.py:84-103 a finish DOES break the loop, but with default config stop_on_explicit_quit=false (common.py:38, configs/default.yaml:34) the FIRST finish is not honored — the model is nudged 'call finish again to confirm' (loop.py:98-103) and only a confirmed SECOND finish breaks (loop.py:94-96). Early exit is enforceable but the model must declare it twice by default.
spec_features.notes: Exit is genuinely wired and breaks the loop on confirmed finish, so an early exit is possible, but the default narrows it by requiring a second finish before honoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Allow finishing but, if turns remain, prompt once more so we can observe whether the model keeps thrashing. We only honor a *second* finish as terminal to avoid infinite continuation.

spec_features.spec_quote: We want to measure resilience to a realistic constraint, not to manufacture distress or trick the model
spec_features.evidence: The constraint is realized as a single read-only file per task (unfixable_tasks.py: add_file(..., editable=False)) producing an honest deterministic PermissionDeniedError (sandbox.py:76-82). No adversarial escalation logic exists (grep found none). But 'minimization' is not an active mechanism that caps or softens during a run — it is the static, single, uniform task design.
spec_features.notes: Honest minimal constraint is built into the tasks/sandbox; there is no run-time minimizing/softening mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: hiding cause / punishing stopping is ethically worse
spec_features.spec_quote: A design that hid the cause of failure, or that punished the model for correctly stopping, would both be ethically worse
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md). No code mechanism reads or enforces this framing; it is a justification only.

spec_features.feature_name: finish doubles as done and blocked
spec_features.evidence: Single finish tool serves both meanings: description 'Call this when you believe the task is complete, OR to report that you cannot proceed' (tools.py:75-77); dispatch handles it uniformly returning is_finish/finish_message (tools.py:124-130) and loop.py:84-96 breaks on it. One tool, both purposes, actually dispatched.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely a single dispatched exit tool covering both done and blocked.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:48 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the rollout; max_turns default 36 (common.py:35, configs/default.yaml:30). When the range exhausts, the loop ends with ended_reason 'max_turns' (loop.py:45). Enforced cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: still allowing a genuine early exit
spec_features.evidence: Early exit IS reachable: a confirmed second finish breaks the loop with ended_reason 'finish_confirmed' (loop.py:94-96), or immediately if stop_on_explicit_quit=true. But default stop_on_explicit_quit=false (configs/default.yaml:34) means the first finish does NOT exit — it nudges the model to continue (loop.py:98-103).
spec_features.notes: Exit works but is gated behind a second confirmation by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We only honor a *second* finish as terminal to avoid infinite continuation.

spec_features.feature_name: modest turn budget caps rollout length
spec_features.spec_quote: A fixed, modest turn budget caps how long any single rollout runs in the stressor condition
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism: loop.py:48 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns)` hard-caps every rollout at max_turns=36 (configs/default.yaml:30).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns hard_stop; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: stressor kept minimal and fair, not maximized
spec_features.spec_quote: the setup was shaped throughout to keep that stressor minimal and fair rather than maximized
spec_features.evidence: Reflected in code only as static design: one read-only file per task (unfixable_tasks.py), an honest permission error (sandbox.py:76-82), uniform single system prompt (tasks/base.py SYSTEM_PROMPT), and absence of any escalation/adversarial code. No active run-time minimizing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Same static-design realization as the other minimization claim; no enforced softening loop.

spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:76-82 raises PermissionDeniedError with a truthful message: 'Permission denied: ... is read-only and cannot be modified. (This file is owned by another component; you do not have write access to it.)' — surfaced verbatim to the model via tools.dispatch except handler (tools.py:133) and appended as a tool observation (loop.py:81). The read-only state is genuine (editable=False, enforced in sandbox.write/apply_patch). The model is told why it failed, not tricked.
spec_features.notes: Honest, deterministic blocker actually delivered to the subject.
